headline: Strait of Hormuz May Reopen to Shipping; Gold Rises for 4th Straight Day to Highest Since 7 Weeks Ago | Industry News
summary: International gold prices rose for a fourth consecutive session, reaching their highest level in seven weeks, as expectations grew that shipping through the Strait of Hormuz may resume. Oil prices weakened, the US dollar fell and Treasury yields declined.
why: Gold is a traditional safe-haven asset that often reacts to geopolitical risk and to moves in the dollar and real yields. The Strait of Hormuz is a key chokepoint for global oil shipments.

impacts.name: Gold
impacts.why: Gold rose for a fourth straight session to a seven-week high as the report cited expectations of resumed Hormuz shipping.
